user.title: Set up Sentinel
user.description: Sentinel centralizes notification handling: recipients, channels and history are configured afterwards from the integration's Configure options.

import_legacy.title: Import K93 ANS
import_legacy.description: An existing K93 ANS setup was found. Sentinel takes it over: recipients, channels, schedules, chatrooms, history and sensor entities are kept. The data folder is copied to /config/sentinel (the old K93-Advanced-Notification-System folder stays as a backup). Update automations and scripts from k93_ans.* to sentinel.* services. Submit to continue.

abort.already_configured: Sentinel is already configured. Only one instance is supported.

data.name: Name
data.send_test: Send a test notification after saving

data_description.person_entity_id: Optional - only meaningful when a notification sets "home only"; required for that filter to affect this recipient at all.
data_description.interactive_entity_id: Optional - a binary_sensor that's "on" while this recipient's phone is in use. Required for the live notification inactivity timeout under Advanced.
data_description.linked_user_id: Optional - the Home Assistant login this recipient's phone belongs to. Required for this recipient to receive a chatroom's new-message-alert push (see Manage chatrooms); has no effect otherwise.
data_description.min_importance: Default minimum importance for this recipient.
data_description.quiet_start: Optional. Between start and end (local time, may cross midnight) only notifications at or above the quiet-hours importance reach this recipient.
data_description.channel_importance: Optional overrides of the minimum importance for single channels, e.g. Security: Low to always get security notifications.
data_description.send_test: Sends a short test push to this recipient's notify service right after saving.

data_description.color: Any CSS color (e.g. #ff0000 or red). Blank = theme default.
data_description.retention_days: Blank = use the global "History retention" under Advanced. Useful for a noisy channel you only want kept a day or two, or an important one you want kept for months.
data_description.max_records: Blank = use the global "History max records" under Advanced. Applies to this channel's own notifications only - a noisy channel's volume no longer crowds out a rarer channel's history.
data_description.labels: Sub-channels to sort this channel's notifications further, e.g. Front door or Garage. Type a name to add one; send_notification's labels field takes the lowercase key (spaces become _).

edit_scheduled.title: Scheduled notification
edit_scheduled.description: Fires send_notification on its own recurring schedule - a cron expression, standard 5-field format (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), e.g. "0 8 * * *" for every day at 08:00, or "*/30 * * * *" for every 30 minutes.

data_description.cron: Standard 5-field cron syntax. Evaluated in Home Assistant's own local time.
data_description.icon: An mdi: icon, e.g. mdi:pill. Blank = default.
data_description.persistent: If true, requires acknowledgement via the built-in persistent notification system, same as send_notification's own "persistent" field.
data_description.home_only: Only deliver to recipients whose assigned person entity is currently home.
data_description.target_recipients: Restrict delivery to these recipients (by name), same as send_notification's own "target_recipients" field. Empty = consider all enabled recipients.
data_description.labels: Labels to attach (defined per channel under Manage channels).
data_description.repeat_minutes: Persistent only: push again every this many minutes until acknowledged. Blank = no repeats.
data_description.repeat_count: Maximum number of repeats. Blank = until acknowledged.

edit_calendar.title: Calendar notification
edit_calendar.description: Fires send_notification when the chosen calendar entity's event becomes active. A normal (timed) event fires as soon as it starts; an all-day event fires at "All-day event time" instead, since Home Assistant reports those active starting at midnight.

data_description.all_day_time: Time of day (local time) an all-day event's notification fires at.
data_description.title: Blank = use the calendar event's own summary.
data_description.message: Blank = use the calendar event's own description (or summary, if it has no description).
data_description.icon: An mdi: icon, e.g. mdi:calendar. Blank = default.
data_description.persistent: If true, requires acknowledgement via the built-in persistent notification system, same as send_notification's own "persistent" field.
data_description.home_only: Only deliver to recipients whose assigned person entity is currently home.
data_description.target_recipients: Restrict delivery to these recipients (by name), same as send_notification's own "target_recipients" field. Empty = consider all enabled recipients.
data_description.labels: Labels to attach (defined per channel under Manage channels).
data_description.repeat_minutes: Persistent only: push again every this many minutes until acknowledged. Blank = no repeats.
data_description.repeat_count: Maximum number of repeats. Blank = until acknowledged.

data_description.icon: An mdi: icon, e.g. mdi:forum. Blank = default.
data_description.allowed_user_ids: Ignored when Access is "All users". Only these users can read this chatroom's history or send messages to it.
data_description.history_max_days: Blank = use the global "Chat history" settings under Advanced.
data_description.history_max_messages: Blank = use the global "Chat history" settings under Advanced.
data_description.new_message_alert: If true, a new message pushes an alert to every other member's phone (via their Recipient's own "Linked user", see Manage recipients) that clears automatically once they read this chatroom. Never shown on the shared notification bell - only ever delivered to members who actually have access.
data_description.navigate_url: Where tapping the new-message-alert notification itself (not an action button) takes you on mobile - a full URL or an app-relative path, e.g. /lovelace-home/chat. Blank = the companion app's own default (opens to its last view).

data_description.chat_history_max_days: Default for a chatroom's own history retention, unless it sets its own override.
data_description.chat_history_max_messages: Default for a chatroom's own history max messages, unless it sets its own override.
data_description.chat_reaction_emoji: The emoji offered when adding a reaction to a chat message. Type any emoji to add it to the list. Removing one here doesn't remove reactions already using it - it only affects what's offered when adding a new one.
data_description.language: Used for outgoing notification text, e.g. the Acknowledge action button.
data_description.live_inactivity_timeout_minutes: 0 = disabled. For notifications sent with interactive_only: true, clears a live notification's push for a recipient once their interactive sensor has been "off" this long.
data_description.storage_path: Blank = default sentinel folder. Absolute, or relative to the Home Assistant config directory; must be writable by Home Assistant. The database.db file inside it is named that regardless. Existing history is migrated automatically. Takes effect as soon as you save.

error.duplicate_key: A channel with this key already exists.
error.unknown: Unexpected error saving - check the Home Assistant log for details.
error.unknown_notify_service: This notify service doesn't exist (yet), so the test notification can't be sent.

legacy_integration_folder.title: Remove the old K93 ANS integration folder
legacy_integration_folder.description: Sentinel has taken over the K93 ANS configuration. The old integration files are still in {path}. Delete that folder and restart Home Assistant.

send_notification.name: Send notification
send_notification.description: Sends a notification through Sentinel. It is fanned out to configured recipients and channels according to their filters, and optionally created as a persistent notification requiring acknowledgement. Returns the notification id (and the recipients it was pushed to) when called with a response variable.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: An mdi: icon shown as the notification's small icon/glyph. If it's not an mdi: icon (and "image" is not set), it's used as the picture instead, for backward compatibility - prefer the separate "image" field for pictures going forward.

image.name: Image
image.description: A picture to attach to the notification: an image URL, or an HA-relative path such as /local/... or /api/camera_proxy/.... Shown as the picture on companion-app push notifications, embedded in the message (as markdown) when "persistent" is true, and shown as a preview in the Lovelace card.

image_entity.name: Image entity
image_entity.description: A camera or image entity to snapshot for the picture instead of supplying "image" directly. Saved under /config/www/sentinel/notifications/<channel>/, uniquely named per capture, and served back as an "image" path automatically. Ignored if "image" is also given - an explicit "image" always wins. Old captures are cleaned up automatically once no stored notification references them anymore.

channel.name: Channel
channel.description: Configured channel key, or a list of them. Built-in channels are info, alert, event, reminder, security, system and chat. When several are given, a recipient receives the notification if it's subscribed to any one of them; the first channel is used for anything that can only carry one value (Android's notification channel, the card's icon color). Defaults to "default".

labels.name: Labels
labels.description: Optional label key, or a list of them, to sort the notification further inside its channel (a "sub-channel"). Labels are defined per channel under Manage channels; cards can filter on them. Unknown labels are kept as-is.

actions.name: Actions
actions.description: List of action buttons, each with "action" and "title" keys.

persistent.name: Persistent
persistent.description: If true, requires acknowledgement via the built-in persistent notification system.

data.name: Data
data.description: Arbitrary extra fields passed through to notify.* targets.

target_recipients.name: Target recipients
target_recipients.description: Restrict delivery to these recipients only, given by their configured name (as shown in Manage Recipients) or their id. Case-insensitive. Omit to consider all recipients.

home_only.name: Home only
home_only.description: Only deliver to recipients whose assigned person entity is currently "home". Recipients with no person assigned are unaffected and always considered.

live_id.name: Live ID
live_id.description: A stable id you choose (e.g. "vacuum_kitchen"). Calling send_notification again with the same live_id updates that same notification in place - same persistent notification, same phone push (via a shared tag), same history row - instead of creating a new one each time. Useful for a repeatedly-updated status notification (e.g. live vacuum-cleaning stats/map). Call end_live_notification with the same live_id when the live session is over to dismiss and clear it everywhere.

interactive_only.name: Interactive only
interactive_only.description: If true, this live notification's push is auto-cleared for any recipient whose "interactive" entity (see Manage Recipients) has been off longer than the Advanced "Live notification inactivity timeout". Defaults to false (delivered and kept regardless of recipient interactivity). Meaningless without both live_id and a recipient's interactive entity being set, and without that Advanced timeout being non-zero.

source.name: Source
source.description: Free-text label for what triggered this notification.

show_in_history.name: Show in history
show_in_history.description: If false, this notification is excluded from the card's History list and ticker, and from the "stored"/"sent" diagnostic sensors. It's still delivered, still counted in Unacknowledged while outstanding, and can still be acknowledged/ended normally - use this for frequent or transient updates (e.g. a live status notification) you don't want cluttering history. Defaults to true.

dismiss_on_action.name: Dismiss on action
dismiss_on_action.description: If false (default), pressing an action button other than Acknowledge (e.g. a vacuum's Pause/Resume) keeps the companion-app notification open instead of closing it, by marking it "sticky". Set to true to restore the old behavior where any action press dismisses the notification. Ignored (always kept open) when "persistent" is true.

clear_on_acknowledge.name: Clear on acknowledge
clear_on_acknowledge.description: If true (default), acknowledging this notification - from the card, the sentinel.acknowledge service, or the phone's own Acknowledge button - also clears the pushed notification on every companion-app recipient it reached. Set to false to leave the phone notification in place even after it's been acknowledged elsewhere.

repeat_minutes.name: Repeat every (minutes)
repeat_minutes.description: Push the notification again every this many minutes until it's acknowledged. Only for persistent notifications; quiet hours still apply to each repeat.

repeat_count.name: Repeat at most
repeat_count.description: Maximum number of repeats. Leave empty to repeat until acknowledged.

acknowledge.name: Acknowledge
acknowledge.description: Marks a notification as acknowledged and dismisses its persistent notification, if any.

notification_id.name: Notification ID
notification_id.description: The id of the notification to acknowledge.

end_live_notification.name: End live notification
end_live_notification.description: Ends a live notification started via send_notification's live_id field: dismisses its persistent notification (if any), clears the pushed notification on every companion-app recipient it reached, and marks it acknowledged so it moves out of the Unacknowledged list. A no-op if no active live notification exists for that live_id.

live_id.name: Live ID
live_id.description: The live_id used in the send_notification calls to update.

delete_notification.name: Delete notification
delete_notification.description: Permanently deletes one notification from history. If it's still outstanding (persistent and not yet acknowledged), its persistent notification is dismissed and any pushed companion-app notification is cleared first, so nothing is left dangling with no history entry behind it.

notification_id.name: Notification ID
notification_id.description: The id of the notification to delete.

clear_history.name: Clear history
clear_history.description: Deletes multiple notifications from history at once. By default only ones that aren't still actively pending acknowledgement are removed (the same rule the History section itself uses), so a still-outstanding notification is never silently lost - set include_unacknowledged to also delete those.

include_unacknowledged.name: Include unacknowledged
include_unacknowledged.description: If true, also delete notifications that still require acknowledgement and haven't gotten it yet.

restore_config_from_snapshot.name: Restore config from snapshot
restore_config_from_snapshot.description: Replaces the ENTIRE current configuration (recipients, channels, scheduled and calendar notifications, Advanced settings) with the contents of config.json - the backup snapshot Sentinel writes automatically alongside database.db on every Configure save. Intended for recovery if the config entry itself is ever lost or corrupted, not routine use. Admin only. The integration reloads immediately afterward, same as saving through Configure would.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be set to true to actually perform the restore - a safety check against calling this by accident, since it overwrites everything currently configured.

send_chat_message.name: Send chat message
send_chat_message.description: Posts a message into a chatroom (see Manage chatrooms). Meant for automations/scripts, not real user-to-user chat - that's what the sentinel-chat-card's own composer is for. Setting sender_name and/or sender_icon posts as that System/bot-style identity regardless of who or what triggered the call - including a manual test from Developer Tools. Leave both blank to instead attribute the message to whichever real Home Assistant user triggered the call (e.g. a script you ran yourself), the same as one sent from the card; falls back to a plain "System" identity if the call has no real user behind it either (e.g. a purely time/state-triggered automation). Non-admin users can only post to chatrooms they have access to.

chatroom_id.name: Chatroom
chatroom_id.description: The chatroom to post to, given by its id or its configured name (as shown in Manage chatrooms), case-insensitively.

sender_name.name: Sender name
sender_name.description: Only used when this call has no real Home Assistant user behind it (see above). Defaults to "System" if left blank.

sender_icon.name: Sender icon
sender_icon.description: Only used when this call has no real Home Assistant user behind it (see above). An mdi: icon. Defaults to mdi:robot if left blank.
